# Structural Regularities of Cinema SDR-to-HDR Mapping in a Controlled Mastering Workflow: A Pixel-wise Case Study on ASC StEM2
**Authors**: Xin Zhang, Xiaoyi Chen
**Year**: 2026
**URL**: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.06276v1

## Abstract Summary
This paper presents an empirical case study on cinema SDR-to-HDR mapping utilizing the ASC StEM2 dataset, which comprises EXR scene-referred images and corresponding SDR/HDR cinema release masters from a consistent ACES-based mastering workflow. Through pixel-wise statistical analysis over 18,580 frames, the study characterizes luminance and color structural relationships across EXR source, SDR, and HDR masters. It finds a highly stable global monotonic luminance correspondence between SDR and HDR masters, with largely consistent geometric structure and localized deviations in highlights and specific materials. The authors define a pixel-level decision map separating EXR-closer recovery regions (82.4%) from content-adaptive adjustment regions, offering a quantitative baseline for structure-aware SDR-to-HDR analysis and learning-based model design under shared-source mastering conditions [1].

## Key Contributions

*   Proposes a pixel-level decision map, classifying 82.4% of sampled regions as EXR-closer recovery and the remainder as requiring adaptive adjustment [1].
*   Offers an interpretable quantitative baseline for structure-aware SDR-to-HDR analysis and the design of learning-based models [1].

# Measurement of the Capillary Length for the Dendritic Growth of Ammonium Chloride
**Authors**: Andrew Dougherty
**Year**: 2012
**URL**: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1206.4030v2

## Abstract Summary
The paper reports on a novel method developed to measure the capillary length for the dendritic crystal growth of non-faceted materials. This new technique involves holding a nearly spherical crystal in unstable equilibrium within an oscillating temperature field. Applying this method to the growth of ammonium chloride crystals from an aqueous solution, the study found the product of the diffusion constant and capillary length ($D d_0$) to be $0.78 \pm 0.07 \,\mathrm{μm^3/s}$. This value is consistent with results obtained for ammonium bromide crystals and significantly refines previous published estimates for ammonium chloride, which varied by over a factor of 20 [3].

**Year**: 2020
**URL**: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.03654v1

## Abstract Summary
This paper describes a reproducible flux method for growing single crystals of iridates, including Sr2IrO4, Sr3Ir2O7, and SrIrO3, at temperatures significantly below the boiling point of the SrCl2 solvent. Traditionally, iridate crystal growth occurs above the solvent's boiling point, leading to non-equilibrium conditions and reduced crucible lifespan. The authors demonstrate that the yield of different iridate phases is highly dependent on the nutrient/solvent ratio, given fixed soak temperature and cooling rate. This low-temperature approach generally results in a lower temperature-independent contribution to magnetic susceptibility than previously reported. For SrIrO3 crystals, paramagnetic behavior can be accurately fitted with a Curie-Weiss law, yielding physically reasonable parameters unlike prior reports. The method not only provides more stable and controllable growth conditions but also extends the lifetime of expensive platinum crucibles and reduces corrosion of furnace components, thereby lowering growth costs [4].
